intro.html:
A limit does not hold the whole widget, it holds one point of it - and alignX and alignY say which one, as a fraction of the widget's box: 0 is its left/top edge, 0.5 its middle, 1 its right/bottom edge. They are the same two numbers a snap grid uses, and they are what x and y mean in a condition too.

All three pieces below have the very same rectangle, drawn around them - only the point it holds differs. Drag each of them into every corner of its frame.

piece1.css: background: #e4572e; border-radius: 12px; color: white; font-size: 20px; text-align: center; line-height: 80px;

code1.css: font-size: 18px; font-family: monospace; white-space: pre-wrap; line-height: 1.35; background: rgba(0,0,0,0.28); border-radius: 8px; padding: 10px;

note1.text: No alignX/alignY, so the limit holds the top left corner - what dragLimit has always done. The corner reaches all four sides of the frame, which leaves the piece hanging out of it at the right and at the bottom by its own width and height.

piece2.css: background: #3b82f6; border-radius: 12px; color: white; font-size: 20px; text-align: center; line-height: 80px;

code2.css: font-size: 18px; font-family: monospace; white-space: pre-wrap; line-height: 1.35; background: rgba(0,0,0,0.28); border-radius: 8px; padding: 10px;

note2.text: The middle of the piece is held instead, so it sticks out of the frame by half its size on every side and the same rectangle is now symmetrical. This is the point most conditions are about: a circle written around 800/500 is where the middle of the piece can go.

piece3.css: background: #3fa34d; border-radius: 12px; color: white; font-size: 20px; text-align: center; line-height: 80px;

code3.css: font-size: 18px; font-family: monospace; white-space: pre-wrap; line-height: 1.35; background: rgba(0,0,0,0.28); border-radius: 8px; padding: 10px;

note3.text: Now the bottom right corner is held, so the piece can never cross the right or the bottom side of the frame and hangs out of it at the top and at the left instead. In Edit Widgets, Position > Drag limits offers these nine points as the "Limited point" picker.
